data.heading: Outcome
data.description: Employees get IT help 24/7 through one conversation, repetitive service interactions are deflected, and escalations reach specialists with context and diagnostic information attached.

blocks.title: Client & industry
blocks.body: Global engineering software enterprise, with IT support spread across multiple systems, knowledge repositories, and specialist teams

blocks.title: Engagement
blocks.body: An agentic front door built as the intelligent first point of interaction between employees and enterprise IT services

blocks.title: Coverage
blocks.body: 24/7, handling Tier 0 and much of Tier 1 support across knowledge, troubleshooting, incidents, and requests

data.heading: Where it started
data.description: Modern enterprises expect IT services to be as simple and responsive as consumer digital experiences, yet employees still navigate portals, search knowledge bases, raise tickets, and wait for support teams to resolve routine issues.

blocks.title: Business problem
blocks.body: Employees navigated complex IT portals, searched fragmented knowledge sources, repeated information across interactions, and waited on routine issues. Support outside traditional service hours was limited, and the experience varied across IT services.

blocks.title: Technical barriers
blocks.body: Enterprise IT support ran across multiple systems, knowledge repositories, service processes, and specialist teams. Issues that guided troubleshooting could have resolved still escalated, adding to service desk workload and lengthening resolution cycles.

blocks.title: Agivant's role
blocks.body: Multi-agent architecture, conversational experience design, ITSM integration, and knowledge and escalation workflows

data.heading: What Agivant built
data.description: Agivant built the front door on a multi-agent architecture, with specialized agents collaborating on each request. It understands intent, reasons over enterprise knowledge, orchestrates the right agents, executes supported IT actions, escalates with context when a person is needed, and learns from every outcome. Value in days and weeks.

blocks.title: Orchestrator agent
blocks.body: Determines the right path, coordinates the other agents, and manages the whole interaction.

blocks.title: Knowledge and guidance agent
blocks.body: Provides trusted answers from enterprise knowledge sources.

blocks.title: Troubleshooting agent
blocks.body: Guides employees through contextual diagnostic and resolution workflows.

blocks.title: Service operations agent
blocks.body: Supports ITSM processes such as incidents, requests, and service interactions.

blocks.title: Expert agent
blocks.body: Brings together deeper technical context, operational signals, and specialized enterprise capabilities.

blocks.title: Context-aware escalation
blocks.body: Hands the interaction to a person with relevant context and diagnostic information.

blocks.title: Learning loop
blocks.body: Captures outcomes and feedback to improve knowledge quality, agent performance, and the service experience.

rows.label: Knowledge
rows.value: Enterprise knowledge sources and troubleshooting guidance

rows.label: Service integration
rows.value: ITSM incidents, requests, and service interactions

rows.label: Grounding data
rows.value: The client's unified operational data platform

blocks.title: Before
blocks.body: Complex portals, fragmented knowledge, repeated information, waits on routine issues, and support limited to service hours.

blocks.title: After
blocks.body: One conversational front door with agent-driven reasoning and routing, direct IT actions, and context-aware handoffs, available 24/7.

data.heading: Proof in production
data.description: An employee describes an issue in plain language. The orchestrator identifies the intent and routes it to the troubleshooting agent, which reasons over enterprise knowledge and guides the employee to a resolution. If the issue needs an incident, the service operations agent raises it, and if it needs a specialist, the handoff carries the context and diagnostics so the employee does not repeat anything.

blocks.heading: Measured results
blocks.description: Repetitive requests stay out of the service desk queue, and specialists get better-quality information at the point of escalation.

blocks.title: Reusable asset
blocks.body: As more agents, enterprise systems, service actions, and operational data sources connect, the front door expands from AI-assisted support to increasingly autonomous service operations. Every build amplifies the next.

blocks.title: Challenges overcome
blocks.body: Bringing multiple systems, knowledge repositories, and specialist teams behind one conversation, keeping the experience consistent across different IT services, and handing over to people without losing context.
